title: Stefan Yasin - Writing
description: Field notes on technical operations, infrastructure, and applied AI.

items.title: How to check whether a Python package is malicious
items.summary: A backdoored LiteLLM release shipped a credential stealer in site-packages. The checks I run before and after installing a dependency.

items.title: Alert severity that people actually respect
items.summary: Most alerting systems have too many levels and no owners. The four-tier severity model I use, with ack windows and escalation timers.

items.title: Monitoring a homelab you cannot always reach
items.summary: Silent failures cost the most. What to watch in a remote lab, what to ignore, and the outside-in heartbeat that catches a dead monitoring host.

items.title: What a $0 home lab taught me about enterprise ops
items.summary: Break things on purpose so production stays boring: the cost discipline, failure modes, and transferable lessons of running a lab on leftovers.

items.title: From Apple Genius to building AI ops tooling
items.summary: Explaining tech to humans in 2014 turned out to be the same skill as building systems that explain themselves in 2026.

items.title: Why I open-source my monitoring tools
items.summary: Abandoned tools, fake claims, and why MIT with an honest README beats marketing. What open source actually gets you when nobody is watching.

items.title: How I cut incident response from hours to minutes
items.summary: Collect, enrich, route, escalate. How I rebuilt alerting across a multi-site manufacturing operation.

items.title: Backporting modern health monitoring onto 2016-era servers
items.summary: A testable decision core behind a thin hardware layer: rackpulse on old Dell PowerEdge and ESXi 6.7.

items.title: Running an AI-assisted ops stack on a near-zero budget
items.summary: Three tools that talk to each other beat eight that don't. The agent stack my job hunt and my lab run on.

items.title: The solar-powered lab that simulates a data center
items.summary: A 40GbE backbone, whole-home automation, and why the lab is the best interview prep I know.
